source_snapshot.title: fix(ingest): resolve renamed type imports, with a default-import guard
source_snapshot.body:
Carries **@Hiro-Chiba's #434** plus one review fix. Landing it here closes #434 as merged.

> ⚠️ **Merge with a merge commit, not squash.** This branch contains Hiro-Chiba's commit alongside mine; a squash would collapse an external contributor's work into one commit authored by me.

## Their change (`819d67e`)

Resolves renamed consumer-side TS bindings for inheritance and type references — `import { Base as LocalBase }` now resolves `EXTENDS`/`REFERENCES`/`CALLS` to the provider's real symbol.

## My fix (`eab1075`)

The fallback matched `binding.imported` against every parsed symbol in the provider file. For `import run from "./m"`, `binding.imported` is the literal sentinel `'default'` (set at `index.ts:514`), not an export name — and `fileHasSymbol` holds every entity including non-exported methods. So any provider member *called* `default` satisfied it:

```
/repo/m.ts  export class M { default() { return 1; } }
            export default new M();
/repo/n.ts  import run from "./m"; export function go() { return run(); }
```

main emits nothing; #434 emits `CALLS go -> m.ts` with `dstQualifiedKey: "M.default"` at **0.9** — confident, and wrong. Guarded with the same `!== 'default'` exclusion `index.ts:3199` already uses.

CI was green because every existing default-import test uses a *named* default export, which resolves before the fallback is reached.

## Verification

Mutation-tested: delete the guard and the added test alone goes red. `tsc --noEmit` clean; core-ingestion shows the same 6 pre-existing fixture-missing failures as the untouched base.

Reviewed as part of a full pass over all 9 open PRs; the per-PR findings and a security review of the combined tree are in the thread on #434.

commits.message:
fix(ingest): don't bind a default import to a member named default

The renamed-import fallback matched `binding.imported` against every parsed
symbol in the provider file. For `import run from "./m"`, `imported` is the
literal sentinel 'default' rather than an export name, so any provider member
that happens to be *called* `default` — a method, getter, or static — satisfied
the lookup and produced a confident (0.9) edge to the wrong member.

Guard the fallback with the same `!== 'default'` exclusion already used when
building rename bindings. Named renamed imports, the case this PR exists to
fix, are unaffected: they short-circuit through filePublicNames.

Existing default-import coverage all used a named default export
(`export default actualName`), which resolves before the fallback — hence the
green suite.

comments.body:
Found and independently verified an additional ingest correctness regression in the current #443 implementation: a renamed import (`import { Base as LocalBase } from "./m"`) falls back to any symbol in the provider file — including a class method — so `extends LocalBase` emits a confident wrong EXTENDS edge to `M.Base` (@0.9), where the PR base never emitted one. The same happens for `import { type User as ExternalUser }`, which emits REFERENCES to `M.User`.

The issue is still reproducible against the current upstream PR state (head `eab1075`), and I did not find an existing fix or duplicate PR addressing it.

Follow-up commit `cba11a3` applies the minimal fix — require a plain module-level key for the renamed-import fallback binding (a member can never be a module export) — and adds regression coverage for the renamed EXTENDS and renamed REFERENCES cases.

Verification: resolveEdges 70/70 on the fix tree, `tsc` clean; the wrong edges reproduce against `eab1075` and are eliminated after.

Follow-up commit:
https://github.com/Alot1z/Ix-remap/commit/cba11a3363b1fbe57819381f05490d2f395674cd

This is ready for the PR author/maintainer to review/cherry-pick.
